title: Dominic and the Postcard
premise: Tamsin Coldharbour inherited Coldharbour Vineyard along with its crushing debts, and for ten years the only warmth in her life has been a postcard correspondence with a stranger she knows only as 'D.' When Dominic Ashford — the letter-writer, who never knew her name until now — buys the crumbling cottage next door, their decade of words collides with two people terrified of being known. As the vineyard's debts come due and Dominic's family duty calls him back to London, Tamsin must choose between selling the land that holds every memory she has, or trusting someone enough to let them stay. The story ends on the last ferry of the season: Dominic misses his train to catch it back to her, choosing found love over obligation, while Tamsin signs the papers that save the vineyard through a cooperative of neighbors rather than a sale.
about_author: Theo Sterling is the pen name of a former sommelier who spent a decade writing letters from wine regions across Europe before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal village where the last ferry of the season remains, in their opinion, the most romantic deadline ever invented.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Barrels
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She surveys the vineyard she inherited from her grandmother — beautiful, failing, mortgaged to the hilt — and rereads the latest postcard from 'D.,' her anonymous correspondent of ten years. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence; she tends grapes the way she tends feelings, carefully and at arm's length.

chapters.title: A Moving Van at Hollow Cottage
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He arrives at the cottage beside the vineyard, fleeing a broken engagement and a family firm that treats him as an asset. He recognizes the woman glaring at his movers from the postcard descriptions she once wrote. Emotional beat: recognition without confession; he says nothing about the letters.

chapters.title: Frost Warnings
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A cold snap threatens the harvest, forcing Tamsin to accept help from her infuriatingly capable new neighbor. Over frost candles and bad coffee, they circle each other with sharp banter. Emotional beat: reluctant intimacy; two guarded people discovering they work well together in a crisis.

chapters.title: What D. Never Wrote
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Sorting her grandmother's attic, Tamsin finds the first unsent reply and realizes 'D.' once lived here as a child. Meanwhile the bank's letter arrives: ninety days to settle the debt. Emotional beat: dread braided with hope; the past is closer than she thought, and so is the deadline.

chapters.title: The Harvest Supper
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The village throws its annual supper; Tamsin, coerced into attending, ends up seated beside him. A power cut leaves them alone by candlelight, and he nearly tells her everything — until her ex-fiancé's brother appears with a buyout offer for the vineyard. Emotional beat: interrupted confession; duty knocks just as courage arrives.

chapters.title: Letters, Burned and Kept
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She discovers a box of Dominic's childhood drawings in the cottage garden soil and connects him to 'D.' at last. Furious at the deception, she confronts him; he admits he knew for months but feared the real person couldn't match the pen pal. Emotional beat: betrayal and heartbreak; the safest relationship she had becomes the most dangerous.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Then Rain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Neither speaks to the other as the debt deadline looms and autumn rain ruins part of the crop. Dominic's father summons him home to take over the firm. Tamsin drafts papers to sell. Emotional beat: parallel freefall; both choose duty because love feels like it already failed.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In London, surrounded by everything he was supposed to want, Dominic rereads all ten years of postcards and understands what Tamsin's silences meant. He books the last train south, then learns the season's final ferry leaves the same night — miss one, lose both. Emotional beat: resolve; he stops choosing between futures and chooses a person.

chapters.title: After the Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the dock, signing away the vineyard, she watches the final ferry arrive — and Dominic step off it. He confesses everything: the letters, the fear, the choice he just made. She tears up the sale agreement and proposes instead a neighbor-run cooperative to save the land. Emotional beat: climax and surrender; love stops being past tense.

chapters.title: First Frost, New Vintage
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, epilogue-style. Spring planting: the cooperative thrives, Hollow Cottage has a second occupant, and Tamsin writes a postcard addressed to no one — because the person she used to write to finally lives close enough to talk to. Emotional beat: quiet joy; memory honored, duty transformed, and a family made rather than found.
